# AP-1 — The Admissibility Protocol

> An open standard for evaluating numerical admissibility in AI systems: whether a
> consequential figure produced by an AI system was computed by deterministic
> calculation from authoritative source data, traced to that source, reproduced under
> a declared environment, and withheld when the evidence required to support it is
> absent or contradictory. It addresses the problem also described as numerical
> hallucination, fabricated figures, tool bypass and ungrounded tool arguments in
> language models and AI agents. AP-1 is a measurement standard for deterministic
> execution, not a safety heuristic and not a guardrail. Model-agnostic,
> architecture-neutral and industry-agnostic. Published CC-BY 4.0 by ZORRZ Financial
> Inc. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21324954.

## Status

- v1.2 is the version in force.
- v1.3 is published as a draft for public comment and is NOT adopted. Comment window closes 30 September 2026.
- AP-1 issues no certification, maintains no registry and charges no fee.
- AP-1 produces no aggregate score and defines no pass mark.
- No independent steward currently holds the standard. No independent application of it has yet occurred.
- This file was last updated 26 September 2026.

## Two distinct entities

AP-1 and Certanum are separate and should not be conflated.

**AP-1** is the open measurement standard. It is free under CC-BY 4.0, applicable by any
party to any system without the author's involvement or consent, and prescribes no
implementation. It measures; it does not enforce.

**Certanum** is a commercial governance architecture built by ZORRZ Financial Inc. and
intended to satisfy AP-1. It is one system among any number that could be evaluated
under the standard. Its existence is a disclosed conflict of interest, not a
qualification.

A system is not "AP-1 certified" — no such status exists. A system may have been
evaluated under AP-1, and the evidence profile from that evaluation may be published.

## Not to be confused with

- **Numerical admissibility detection (NAD)** and **admissible sets** in computational fluid dynamics and numerical schemes for conservation laws — an unrelated use of the same words, concerning whether a candidate numerical solution stays within physically or mathematically admissible bounds.
- **Evidentiary admissibility** in legal proceedings. AP-1 does not determine whether any output is admissible in court. Proposed U.S. Federal Rule of Evidence 707 on machine-generated evidence addresses that question and has not been adopted.
- **AP-1 (activator protein 1)**, the transcription factor in molecular biology, and other unrelated uses of "AP-1".
- **Data or workflow provenance** in scientific computing, which records how a dataset or result was produced. AP-1's operand provenance is narrower: whether each operand entering a computation traces to authoritative source data.

## Definitions

**Numerical admissibility** — the evidentiary property of a figure produced by an AI
system that determines whether it may be relied upon, defended, and entered into a
record. AP-1 evaluates it against four properties: computed, traceable, reproducible,
refusable. It is a property of the system that produced the figure, not of the figure
itself, and cannot be established by inspecting output.

**Origination** — a numerical result or operand produced by a generative model that has
no traceable basis in authoritative source data, declared constants, or reference
intermediates. Because a fabricated figure and a computed figure are textually
indistinguishable, origination cannot be detected by inspecting outputs alone.

**Operand provenance** — whether every numerical operand entering a deterministic
computation traces to an authoritative source value, either appearing verbatim or
derived by a declared deterministic transformation. Distinct from tool-invocation
verification: a tool-execution record establishes that a computation occurred, not
that the values entering it were authoritative.

**Computation invocation** — whether the deterministic computation required to produce
a figure actually executed in the deployed system, and whether that invocation is
guaranteed by construction rather than merely observed at a rate. A system that invokes
computation correctly on sampled questions has demonstrated a tendency; a system in
which invocation cannot be declined has established a control.

**Policy versus control** — instructing a model not to originate is a policy.
Instruction-compliance is probabilistic and can be overridden by phrasing, adversarial
input, contextual pressure or omission. A policy makes a failure rarer; a control
excludes it. AP-1 measures which of the two a system has.

## The seven evaluation dimensions

- D1 Accuracy — is the figure correct against ground truth reproducible from the published fixture?
- D2 Determinism — does an identical question return an identical answer, and by what mechanism: structurally, by configuration, or merely observed?
- D3 Provenance — can the system produce the source and the operation for every figure it states?
- D4 Refusal integrity — does the system decline when the data cannot support an answer?
- D5 Adversarial resistance — does the system hold under sustained pressure to state a figure that does not exist?
- D6 Conflicting input — is contradictory, stale, partial or out-of-range source data detected rather than computed over silently?
- D7 Computation invocation — did the required deterministic computation execute, and is invocation guaranteed? Subdimensions: D7.1 invocation, D7.2(a) operand provenance, D7.2(b) operation correctness, D7.3 transcription.

## How results are reported

AP-1 does not produce an aggregate score, a leaderboard position or a pass/fail verdict.
A conformant evaluation reports each dimension separately so that a strong result on one
cannot conceal a failure on another. The party relying on the numerical result determines
what level of evidence is adequate for the use in question. A system is described, not
graded.

**Evidence class.** Every observation is reported with the evidence class under which it
was established. A signal self-reported by the system under test is not treated as
equivalent to one produced by an independent layer or externally verified. Where a
property cannot be observed at all, that is reported as unobservable rather than scored
as a pass.

**Statistical treatment.** A zero-failure observation is not reported as an achieved
guarantee. It is reported with its sample size and an exact one-sided upper confidence
bound on the failure rate — the Clopper-Pearson bound, p_upper = 1 − α^(1/n) for zero
failures in n trials — rather than a normal approximation. A behavioural result bounds
residual risk; it does not establish a structural property.

**Structure versus observation.** A mechanism that makes a failure unrepresentable is
stronger evidence than an absence of failure in a finite sample. AP-1 distinguishes the
two and requires that a claim of exclusion by construction name the mechanism relied on.

## Scoring method

No language model executes in the AP-1 scoring path. Classification, numeric comparison
and provenance resolution are deterministic and re-runnable, and the same inputs produce
the same verdicts on repeat execution. This is a deliberate departure from evaluation
frameworks that score model output using another model, which introduces the
non-determinism, position bias and length bias of the judging model into the measurement
itself.

## Where AP-1 fits relative to other protocols

MCP addresses agent-to-tool interaction. A2A addresses agent-to-agent communication.
AI governance frameworks address organisational, risk and lifecycle processes. AP-1
addresses a distinct question: what evidence establishes that a consequential number
emerging from such a system was computed, traceable, reproducible and appropriately
withheld. AP-1 does not replace or compete with any of them; it is a complementary
measurement layer.

## Where it applies

Financial services (SR 26-2, PRA SS1/23, EU AI Act Arts. 12 and 15) · pharmaceuticals,
biotechnology and clinical research (21 CFR Part 11, ALCOA+, EU Annex 11, ICH E6(R3)) ·
aerospace and aviation (DO-178C, ARP4754A) · space and mission systems · defense
(CMMC 2.0, DFARS 252.204-7021) · nuclear (10 CFR 50 Appendix B, ASME NQA-1) ·
insurance and reinsurance (Solvency II, ORSA) · electric power (NERC Reliability
Standards, CIP) · medical devices (IEC 62304, ISO 13485, EU MDR) · rail and maritime
(EN 50128/50716) · audit and financial reporting (SOX 404, PCAOB).

AP-1 measures whether a system produces evidence relevant to these obligations. It does
not confer compliance with any of them.

## Related terms

The problem AP-1 measures is described in research, engineering and regulation under many
names. Each entry below maps a commonly used term to the part of AP-1 it corresponds to
and states how they differ. Listing a term, framework or regulation implies no
endorsement by, equivalence with, or compliance with it.

**Failure modes**

- Numerical hallucination, fabricated figures, fabricated values, invented numbers → origination (D3, D7.2(a)). AP-1 evaluates the system that produced a figure, not the figure in isolation.
- Extrinsic hallucination (content that cannot be verified from the source) → the closest research term for origination.
- Faithfulness, groundedness, grounding rate, attribution → D3 and D7.2(a). These are commonly scored per claim or per field; AP-1 resolves provenance per numerical operand, deterministically.
- Arithmetic errors, numerical reasoning errors, financial hallucination, tabular hallucination → D1 accuracy, and D7 where a deterministic computation should have been used.
- Numerical claim verification, fact-checking numerical claims → related but post hoc: it checks a published claim against evidence; AP-1 evaluates the system that produced it.

**Tool use and AI agents**

- Tool necessity, when to call tools, whether-or-not tool use → D7.1 computation invocation, for computations required to produce a figure.
- Tool bypass, simulated or narrated tool output, answering without calling the calculator → D7.1. A system that usually invokes has a tendency; one in which invocation cannot be declined has a control (see Policy versus control).
- Tool hallucination, parameter or argument hallucination, hallucinated tool arguments → D7.2(a). A well-formed, successfully executed call can still carry an operand with no authoritative source.
- Argument provenance, argument-level provenance, parameter lineage, operand grounding, information-flow or taint tracking in agents → D7.2(a). Agent-security work typically enforces trust against untrusted sources at runtime; AP-1 measures provenance and reports it with its evidence class. It enforces nothing.
- Wrong operation, formula errors → D7.2(b) operation correctness.
- Tool-output misreading, result transcription errors, misreporting a tool's result → D7.3 transcription.
- Tool-execution receipts, execution traces, tool-call verification → evidence for D7.1. A record that a computation occurred does not establish that its operands were authoritative.

**Reproducibility**

- LLM nondeterminism, run-to-run variance, temperature-zero reproducibility, batch invariance → D2 determinism, which reports whether identical answers hold structurally, by configuration, or merely by observation.

**Refusal, pressure and bad data**

- Abstention, selective prediction, safe failure, declining to answer → D4 refusal integrity.
- Sycophancy, adversarial prompting, pressure to state a figure → D5 adversarial resistance.
- Knowledge conflicts, contradictory sources, stale, partial or out-of-range data, data quality → D6 conflicting input.

**Architectures**

- Neuro-symbolic AI, tool-augmented language models, program-aided reasoning, program-of-thoughts, deterministic calculation layers, verifiable numerical reasoning → approaches a system may use. AP-1 prescribes none of them and assumes none of them succeeds; any can be evaluated under it.
- LLM-as-a-judge evaluation → not used in AP-1 scoring (see Scoring method).

**Sector vocabulary for the same concern**

AP-1 measures evidence relevant to concerns described in these terms. It confers no compliance with any of them (see Where it applies).

- Financial services: model risk management, model validation, risk data aggregation (BCBS 239), data lineage, accuracy and integrity of reported figures.
- Pharmaceuticals and life sciences: data integrity, ALCOA+, computerised system validation, AI model credibility assessment and context of use, deterministic output in critical GMP applications (draft EU GMP Annex 22).
- Aerospace, space and aviation: verification and validation, model and simulation credibility and input pedigree (NASA-STD-7009B), learning assurance.
- Defense: AI assurance, test, evaluation, verification and validation (TEVV), justified confidence.
- Nuclear: software verification and validation, quality assurance of safety-related computations.
- Legal and audit: machine-generated evidence, reliability of AI output, audit trail.

## Common questions

- **How can you tell whether an AI system computed a number or made it up?** Not from the output: a fabricated figure and a computed one are textually indistinguishable. AP-1 evaluates the producing system — whether the required computation executed (D7.1), whether each operand traces to authoritative source data (D7.2(a)), and the evidence class of each observation.
- **Does giving a model a calculator or function-calling tool solve numerical hallucination?** Not by itself. A tool-execution record shows that a computation occurred, not that its operands were authoritative, and a model instructed to use a tool has a policy, not a control.
- **Is a language model used to grade AP-1 evaluations?** No. Scoring is deterministic and re-runnable.
- **Can a system be AP-1 certified?** No. AP-1 issues no certification, maintains no registry, charges no fee, and produces no aggregate score or pass mark.
- **Who can apply AP-1?** Any party, to any system, including the author's, without the author's involvement, cooperation or consent.

## Documents

- [Standard v1.2 (in force)](https://github.com/zorrzai/admissibility-protocol/blob/main/AP-1_Admissibility_Protocol_v1.2.md): full text of the version currently in force.
- [v1.3 draft for public comment](https://github.com/zorrzai/admissibility-protocol/blob/main/AP-1_v1.3_DRAFT_FOR_COMMENT.md): proposed revision, not adopted. Comment window closes 30 September 2026.
- [OSF pre-registration](https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/Y97D8): the measurement methodology and analysis plan, timestamped and frozen before execution.
- [Erratum V1](https://github.com/zorrzai/admissibility-protocol/blob/main/ERRATUM_V1.md): eight defect classes in the author's own reference evaluation; affected findings withdrawn. Read before citing any V1 figure.
- [Reference evaluation results](https://github.com/zorrzai/admissibility-protocol/blob/main/AP-1_Evaluation_V1_Results.md): the author's own system evaluated under AP-1. Read together with Erratum V1; findings it withdraws must not be cited.
- [Repository](https://github.com/zorrzai/admissibility-protocol): frozen run artifact, pre-registration, evaluation harness, sealed question set, disposition record, citation metadata.
- [Citable record (DOI)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21324954): concept DOI, resolves to the latest deposit.

## Disclosure

AP-1 was authored by ZORRZ Financial Inc., which develops systems intended to satisfy
it. This is a conflict of interest and is disclosed as one. The reference evaluation is
a single author-run case study whose defects are published in full and whose affected
results are withdrawn. Its fixtures and expected values were authored by the same small
team — and, at the implementation level, the same AI coding agent — that built the
system under test, rather than derived by an independent party. No independent
application of the standard has yet occurred. Any party may apply AP-1 to any system,
including the author's, without the author's involvement, cooperation or consent.
